idiom_name: axum Extension<T> / custom FromRequestParts extractor over tower middleware
implementation_notes: Rust has no identity type in std, so the descriptor is an immutable struct you define (subject id, roles, tenant) and attach to the request in tower middleware; handlers read it through an extractor - axum's Extension<T> works when the middleware ran, and a custom FromRequestParts implementation is the way to make absence impossible to ignore because it can reject with 401 instead of failing lazily. Store the descriptor owned (or behind Arc) in request extensions, never a reference into request-scoped buffers, and keep it immutable. The classic authenticator/descriptor/factory structure is replaced by one middleware plus one extractor; reach for the axum-login variant only when you would otherwise re-implement session authentication.
pitfalls: axum's Extension<T> rejects with 500 when the middleware never ran, so a missing auth layer looks like a server bug instead of an unauthenticated request - the custom extractor returning 401 belongs at the boundary.
Extensions must own their data: storing &str borrowed from headers or the body in the descriptor forces lifetimes through the whole handler chain - build an owned Subject.
An Arc<Subject> is cheap to clone but not immutable by itself; keep the struct free of interior mutability or concurrent handlers will observe each other's writes.

variants.name: axum-login AuthSession (session-backed)
variants.implementation_notes: axum-login ships the session-backed realization: implement AuthUser for your descriptor type and AuthnBackend for the store, add the AuthManagerLayer over tower-sessions, and read the AuthSession extractor in handlers (or guard routes with login_required!/permission_required!). The crate keeps the user id in the session and re-loads the descriptor per request, which is exactly the reload policy this pattern wants, so prefer it over rebuilding session authentication by hand.
pitfalls: AuthnBackend::get_user returning an error instead of None turns an expired session into a 500 - distinguish "no user" from "load failed".
session_auth_hash must change when the credential changes (for example on password rotation), otherwise old sessions stay valid after a reset.
AuthSession is only meaningful behind AuthManagerLayer; a route mounted without the layer silently sees no user.
